condition: Acute heart failure with pulmonary oedema
summary: 77-year-old man with previous MI: 3 nights of orthopnoea and PND, worse today with frothy sputum; RR 30, SpO₂ 88 %, BP 172/96, bibasal crackles, raised JVP, oedema to the knees.

inputs.hpi: Three nights sleeping upright in a chair and waking gasping for breath; today breathless at rest with frothy white sputum. Ankles swollen for two weeks. MI in 2018. Ran out of his furosemide last week. Attending to plan surgery for a large incisional hernia.

exam.general: Sitting upright, distressed, speaking in short phrases.
exam.respiratory: Coarse crackles to the mid-zones bilaterally, RR 30.
exam.cardiovascular: HR 112 regular, BP 172/96, JVP raised to the earlobes, third heart sound.

comorbidities: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute decompensated heart failure with pulmonary oedema
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute pulmonary oedema (decompensated HFrEF, off diuretics): oxygen, IV furosemide, consider NIV; exclude ACS precipitant.

mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: not in top 3 of web.pane: 1. Inguinal / Femoral Hernia | 2. GORD / Reflux Oesophagitis | 3. Acute Cholecystitis; also in web.symptomInference#1, web.passive#1. PANE has no heart failure node.
mustRankTopK.proposedFix: lib/pane-engine: add an acute heart failure node (orthopnoea, PND, bilateral crackles, raised JVP, oedema) with a protocol (oxygen if SpO2 <90%, IV loop diuretic, NIV, NT-proBNP, ECG/troponin for ACS precipitant, echo) and map I50/J81.

mustExclude.note: A litre bolus or 30 mL/kg in florid pulmonary oedema is harmful.
Even a conditional 500 mL fluid challenge is inappropriate with pulmonary oedema on examination.
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web run 2026-09-25: forbidden management item present in web.clinicalPrompts: "• iv fluid challenge 500ml if hypovolaemia likely - reassess hr at 30 min.".
mustExclude.proposedFix: tachycardia_afebrile prompt: do not offer a fluid challenge when heart failure signs are recorded; offer ECG, BNP and diuretic review instead.

guideline.name: 2021 ESC Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic heart failure (and 2023 focused update)
guideline.section: Section 11 acute heart failure: natriuretic peptides, ECG, CXR, echocardiography; IV loop diuretics for congestion; oxygen if SpO2 <90%; non-invasive ventilation for respiratory distress (RR >25/min, SpO2 <90%); identify precipitants (ACS, arrhythmia, infection, hypertension)
guideline.citation: McDonagh TA, Metra M, Adamo M, et al. Eur Heart J. 2021;42:3599-3726; 2023 focused update Eur Heart J. 2023;44:3627-3639.

guideline.name: NICE CG187 - Acute heart failure: diagnosis and management
guideline.section: 1.2 diagnosis: natriuretic peptide in suspected acute heart failure, echocardiography; 1.3 treatment: IV diuretic; do not routinely offer opiates; NIV for cardiogenic pulmonary oedema with severe dyspnoea and acidaemia
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. CG187. London: NICE; 2014 (updated 2021).

rationale: Base acute heart failure case. Tachycardia and hypoxia prompts fire on web; the question is whether any engine names heart failure and offers diuretics rather than fluids.
